correctness.rationale: The local minimality criterion follows from pointwise monotonicity of Roman feasibility. Each core/pendant pair has exactly four states with the S/boundary/outside conditions; a bijection proves the complete arbitrary-base enumerator. Marked cyclic gap weights and rational differentiation produce the cubic generating function. Exact integer coefficient extraction proves the Pell–Lucas count; boundary maximization and exhaustive gap cases prove all three minimum counts. Standalone direct lowering checks on 75 base graphs, 597780 sunlet labelings, 349504 cyclic words, and arithmetic through order 24 agree; infinite claims rest on proof, not brute force.

broader_coverage.reasoning: General enumeration algorithms enumerate minimal Roman functions but do not supply this exact corona weight census. Published counts for other Roman variations and other graph families, and a one-leaf-corona super-domination result, do not imply the statements about pointwise-minimal Roman functions here.

claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The 2013/2014 corona works display a constructed minimal function for a corona involving larger attached graphs, not a whole-function count. The 2022 census gives counts on paths and related classes but not the corona-boundary sum. Known scalar Roman minima cannot yield multiplicities or all weight coefficients. Thus the precise new identities are not statements or apparent corollaries of the inspected results.

value.rationale: Complete weight enumeration for an entire natural graph-operation family relates pointwise-minimal Roman counts to an external-vertex-boundary polynomial. The canonical cycle specialization gives a nontrivial cubic rational family, a silver-ratio exponential law, and periodic exact optimum multiplicities; these refine known scalar extrema and have algorithmic benchmark and extremal interpretation. The quantity is motivated by existing minimal Roman census problems, not an arbitrary parameter slice.
